title: Long Pressed Name
statement: Return true if typed can be produced from name by long-pressing some characters, causing repeated characters in typed.
explanation: Advance matching characters in both strings; extra typed characters are allowed only when they repeat the previous name character.

title: Unique Email Addresses
statement: Count unique email addresses after ignoring dots and everything after + in each local part; domains remain unchanged.
explanation: Normalize each local part according to the rules and store the resulting address in a set.

title: Number of Recent Calls
statement: Implement RecentCounter.ping(t), returning the number of calls in the inclusive interval [t-3000,t].
explanation: Append the new timestamp and remove older timestamps until the queue starts at t-3000 or later.

title: Reorder Data in Log Files
statement: Place all letter logs before digit logs; sort letter logs by content then identifier, while keeping digit logs in original order.
explanation: Partition logs by whether the first content token is a digit; sort only letter logs using content and identifier as tie-breaker.
example: logs=["dig1 8 1","let1 art can","dig2 3 6","let2 own kit","let3 art zero"]

title: Range Sum of BST
statement: Return the sum of node values in a BST that lie in the inclusive range [low, high].
explanation: Add in-range values and use BST ordering to skip subtrees that cannot contain in-range values.

title: Valid Mountain Array
statement: Return true if an array strictly increases to one peak and then strictly decreases, with both sides non-empty.
explanation: Walk upward, require a non-endpoint peak, then walk downward and check that the entire array was consumed.

title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted
approach: Check each column top to bottom
statement: Count columns that are not sorted in nondecreasing order from the first row to the last row.
explanation: For each column, mark it for deletion if any character is smaller than the character directly above it.

title: Verifying an Alien Dictionary
approach: Compare adjacent words by custom ranks
statement: Return true if the list of words is sorted according to a supplied alien alphabet order.
explanation: Map each alphabet character to its rank and compare adjacent words at their first differing character, handling prefixes.

title: N-Repeated Element in Size 2N Array
statement: An array of length 2N contains N+1 distinct values, with one value repeated N times; return that repeated value.
explanation: Scan values and return the first one already present in a set.

title: Univalued Binary Tree
approach: Check every node against the root value
statement: Return true if every node in a binary tree has the same value.
explanation: Traverse the tree and reject any node whose value differs from the root value.
